paper.title: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22
paper.research_summary: This work uses pre-trained machine learning models from the Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) framework to interpolate total energy predictions for OER surface intermediates on 4119 oxide materials, then constructs a flexible high-throughput screening framework to identify viable anode catalyst candidates for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) under bulk and nanoscale Pourbaix stability, material cost, overpotential, and metastability constraints.

task.task_name_raw: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER
task.objective: Identify viable candidate anode catalysts for OER under varying reaction conditions for bulk, surface, and nanoscale Pourbaix stability as well as material cost, overpotential, and metastability.
output_goal: 122 and 68 viable candidates for OER under bulk and nanoscale regime respectively

evidence.text: In this work, we interpolated a database of the total energy predictions for all slabs and OER surface intermediates for 4119 oxide materials in the original OC22 dataset using pre-trained models from the OC22 framework. This database includes all terminations of all facets up to a maximum Miller index of 1. To demonstrate the full utility of this database, we constructed a flexible screening framework to identify viable candidate anode catalysts for OER under varying reaction conditions for bulk, surface, and nanoscale Pourbaix stability as well as material cost, overpotential, and metastability.

stages.stage_name_raw: Obtaining bulk materials for slab construction
stages.stage_goal: Acquire bulk oxide materials for slab generation.
stage_output: bulk materials used for slab construction

evidence.text: The bulk materials used for slab construction in this study were obtained from the Materials Project.

stages.stage_goal: Generate slabs for all facets up to maximum Miller index of 1 with all terminations.
stage_output: slabs with atomic and vacuum layers of ca. 12.5 Å thick

evidence.text: We described all facets up to a MMI of 1 containning an atomic and vacuum layer of ca. 12.5 Å thick. The bulk materials used for slab construction in this study were obtained from the Materials Project. We also considered all terminations for each facet (sans slabs exceeding 200 atoms) while maintaining equivalent surfaces on both sides of the slab which consequently resulted in non-stoichiometric slabs with respect to the bulk formula.

stages.stage_goal: Fine-tune the pre-trained S2EF-Total model on OC22 dataset to better predict total energies of oxide surfaces and surface intermediates.

evidence.text: We used a pre-trained model for the Structure to Energy and Forces (S2EF)-Total task from the OC22 framework to perform all machine learning predictions of the relaxed structure and total energy. The entirety of the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset (1281040 DFT relaxations) was used to train an S2EF-Total model which was subsequently fine-tuned with the OC22 dataset (62331 DFT relaxations) to better predict the total energies of oxide surfaces and surface intermediates.

stages.stage_name_raw: Interpolating total energy predictions for slabs and surface intermediates
stages.stage_goal: Interpolate total energy predictions for all slabs and OER surface intermediates for 4119 oxide materials.
stage_output: interpolated database of total energy predictions

evidence.text: Using the previously developed ML models, we systematically extrapolated the total DFT energy of all terminations for all facets up to a MMI = 1 for all 4119 materials considered in this study.

stages.stage_goal: Screen candidates using a set of progressive criteria including Pourbaix stability, Wulff shape analysis, overpotential assessment, energy above hull, and material cost.
stage_output: 122 and 68 viable candidates for OER under bulk and nanoscale regime respectively

evidence.text: Fig. 5 summarizes the selection criteria that we employed to screen for candidate electrocatalysts for OER. The first criteria in our high-throughput screening framework was to determine if a material exists in the original training dataset of OC22. ... The second criterion describes the Pourbaix stability, i.e., the electrochemical stability of a material in aqueous environment. ... The third selection criterion ... assesses the surface energy ... to construct the Wulff shape ... The fourth criterion assesses the overpotential ... The fifth criterion assesses the thermodynamic stability ... The final criterion assesses the material cost ...

stages.stage_goal: Validate ML-predicted Gibbs adsorption energies and overpotentials using DFT calculations.
stage_output: MAE of test set (0.42 eV for Gibbs adsorption energy)

evidence.text: We used DFT to validate 85 values for Gibbs adsorption energy corresponding to eqn (6)–(8) for 33 Pourbaix stable compounds in our database. The MAE of the test set shown in Fig. 7(a) is 0.42 which is larger than the MAE of 0.239 eV obtained from the validation set in the original OC22 assessment.
